subject: mobile-programming
name: Mobile Programming
exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance).

units.title: Mobile Platforms and Application Architecture
topics: The platform you can see: hardware, pixels and screens

sections.title: The platform you can see: hardware, pixels and screens

summary: Android and iOS dominate; native, web, PWA, hybrid and cross-platform approaches trade cost against fidelity.
Android layers: Linux kernel, HAL, native libraries and ART, Java API framework, apps; each app is sandboxed in its own process and can be killed in the background.
iOS layers: Core OS, Core Services, Media, Cocoa Touch; concepts map one-to-one to Android.
Mobile constraints (battery, memory, screens, intermittent network, interruptions) shape design; in Nepal, low-end devices, offline use and Nepali support matter most.
px = dp × dpi/160; image memory = width × height × bytes per pixel; sample down large images.

units.title: Android Components, Intents and the Activity Lifecycle
topics: Tasks, back stack and launch modes
Services, receivers and providers in outline
Seeing the lifecycle: states, stacks and intents

sections.title: Tasks, back stack and launch modes
Services, receivers and providers in outline
Seeing the lifecycle: states, stacks and intents

summary: An app is a set of components (Activity, Service, BroadcastReceiver, ContentProvider) declared in the manifest and started by the system.
Intents are messages; explicit Intents name a class, implicit Intents describe an action matched by intent filters; extras must be small.
The Activity lifecycle (onCreate … onDestroy) is driven by the system; the back stack keeps stopped activities; rotation destroys and recreates the activity.
Survive rotation with ViewModel and onSaveInstanceState; survive everything with persistent storage.
Launch modes control instance reuse; services, receivers and providers have narrow, battery-aware roles.

units.title: User Interface - Layouts, RecyclerView and Fragments
topics: Seeing the interface: tools, trees, lists and panes

sections.title: Seeing the interface: tools, trees, lists and panes

summary: UIs are trees of Views in ViewGroups; ConstraintLayout gives flat, responsive screens; resource qualifiers supply Nepali text, dark mode, tablets and density-specific assets.
All UI work runs on the main thread; blocking it risks an ANR, so I/O goes to background threads.
RecyclerView recycles a handful of ViewHolders (15 here instead of 10,000); DiffUtil computes the minimal list updates (n + m − 2·LCS operations).
Fragments are lifecycle-aware UI pieces; drop view references in onDestroyView; Navigation manages destinations.
Compose describes UI as functions of state.

units.title: Data Storage - Preferences, Files, SQLite and Room
topics: Testing business logic off the device
Seeing where data lives: flash, files, tables and keys

sections.title: Testing business logic off the device
Seeing where data lives: flash, files, tables and keys

summary: Match storage to data: DataStore for settings, files for blobs, Room/SQLite for records, content providers for sharing, a server for the source of truth.
SQL queries use parameter binding; transactions roll back on failure (the executed example left row 1 at 450).
Room provides Entity, DAO and Database with compile-time-checked queries, Flow updates and migrations.
Pure business logic is testable on a JVM (the EMI example); keep Android classes thin.
Encrypt sensitive data and keep secrets off the device.

units.title: Networking, JSON and Background Work
topics: Seeing the network: towers, requests, states and retries

sections.title: Seeing the network: towers, requests, states and retries

summary: HTTP methods, status codes and REST resources; use HTTPS, tokens and timeouts.
JSON is parsed into objects defensively (missing fields, pagination, compression); the sample parse gave 3 items totalling Rs 1570.
Network and disk run off the main thread: coroutines with ViewModel and a Loading/Ok/Error state.
Retry only transient, idempotent failures with exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30 seconds).
WorkManager runs deferrable work reliably under constraints; respect Doze and battery.

units.title: Sensors, Location, Permissions and Notifications
topics: Camera, media and sensors of the environment
Seeing the sensors: chips, satellites, curves and prompts

sections.title: Camera, media and sensors of the environment
Seeing the sensors: chips, satellites, curves and prompts

summary: Permissions are normal, dangerous (runtime), special or signature; ask minimally, in context, with a rationale and a fallback.
Sensors deliver noisy values at chosen rates; unregister listeners in onPause; a magnitude-threshold step detector counted 20 steps in the simulated walk.
Location uses GPS, network and fused providers; the haversine formula gives great-circle distance; trade accuracy against battery.
CameraX, photo picker, QR scanning and Bluetooth/NFC extend the device's reach with their own permissions.
Notifications need channels, a PendingIntent and (recent Android) a runtime permission; FCM delivers push messages.

units.title: Cross-Platform Development, Testing and Publishing
topics: Seeing the release: frameworks, tests, packages and keys

sections.title: Seeing the release: frameworks, tests, packages and keys

summary: Cross-platform frameworks (Flutter, React Native, Kotlin Multiplatform, PWAs) trade one code base against size, fidelity and plugin dependence; choose by team skills and requirements.
Test mostly with fast JVM unit tests, some integration tests and few UI tests; test on low-end devices, slow networks and Nepali locale.
Release as a shrunk (R8) AAB; Play generates device-specific APKs; keep download size low.
Signing proves authorship and integrity; v2 signs chunk digests of the whole file (tampering flips the root digest); protect the key.
versionCode must increase (major × 10,000 + minor × 100 + patch); publish through staged tracks with a complete listing.
